band_vocabulary.meaning: Thermal stress is within the range most healthy adults tolerate.
Rising thermal stress; heat-sensitive groups should start adapting schedules.
Dangerous thermal stress for outdoor exposure; municipal heat actions should activate.
Life-threatening thermal stress possible; emergency heat-health response.

demo_disclaimer: Demo / synthetic scenario — not a live forecast or observation.
how_to_read: Pick a scenario, then read the outlook (lead times), thermal stress (HTSI + quality flags), impact (vulnerability + health-impact status), actions and notification previews. Every value is synthetic and labelled; the physics and the decision rules are the same code that runs on live data.

scenarios.label: Monsoon break — cooler, near-normal stress
scenarios.summary: Pre-monsoon squall line brings cloud, breeze and rain showers. Tmax stays 6–8 °C BELOW the 1991–2020 normal: thermal stress is Normal in most zones and Watch in the densest core. No heatwave candidate fires.
scenarios.tagline: What NORMAL and WATCH conditions look like.
teaching_points: Normal/Watch levels exist so operators can see the quiet state too
Cloud and wind cut the globe temperature — radiation matters, not just Tmax
A below-normal day can still carry modest WBGT in full sun

scenarios.label: Dry extreme heatwave — severe at lead 3–5
scenarios.summary: A dry heat dome builds over the region. Tmax climbs from 43 °C on the issue day to 47.6 °C by Day +4 — departures of +6 to +7.4 °C over the fixed 1991–2020 normal. Days +2 to +5 form a declared SEVERE heatwave episode (≥2-day persistence), so warnings carry real lead time of 3, 4 and 5 days.
teaching_points: Lead times 3/4/5 days on a declared episode — the product's core promise
Two-day persistence rule: the first candidate day stays an early watch
Dry air keeps wet-bulb/WBGT far below the Heat Index — the metrics disagree because they answer different questions

scenarios.label: Humid dangerous heat — WBGT-driven severe risk
scenarios.summary: Moist maritime air keeps Tmax at 35–38 °C — BELOW the IMD heatwave absolute threshold, so no heatwave episode is declared — but humidity of 68–82 % at peak drives estimated WBGT past 33–35 °C and the HTSI into Severe. Sweat stops evaporating; the dry-bulb number hides the danger.
scenarios.tagline: Why temperature alone is not enough.
teaching_points: IMD Tmax label says None/Watch while thermal stress says Severe — read both
Wet-bulb physics: humidity dominates WBGT when radiation is modest
Health-impact indicator escalates from the thermal channel, not the heatwave channel

scenarios.label: Severe heat + hazardous air pollution
scenarios.summary: A stagnant, near-windless spell traps dust and combustion PM2.5 under strong heat. Tmax approaches 48 °C in the densest zones (a severe heatwave episode on Days +2 to +5) WHILE PM2.5 peaks push the indicative Indian AQI into the 400s. The joint heat+air load band reaches Severe, lifting recommended actions a level.
scenarios.tagline: Compound exposure: the joint heat+air load escalates.
teaching_points: Concentration AQI stays separate from the parameterised joint load
Stagnant wind raises both WBGT (less convective cooling) and PM2.5
Escalation rule: severe air load + thermal ≥ warning ⇒ severe alert level
